rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24, D3 of bugs_closed/305: "`rather than` is a little bit of a tic."

WHY THAT NEEDED A DESIGN DECISION RATHER THAN A FLAG. D3 was framed with two answers: it is a tic (repair it like the rest) or it is ordinary English (drop it from the trip family, keep it as a density signal). The ruling is neither - it is the middle - so implementing it meant deciding WHAT the middle acts on.

WHAT THE BUDGET ACTUALLY IS, because this is the part that made the answer obvious once read correctly. `page_budget` (default 2) is NOT a cap on repairs. It is a TOLERANCE: the first N non-exempt non-headline hits on a page are left alone and everything after them is repaired. So the scarce resource the gate allocates is not repair effort, it is FORGIVENESS. (I had this backwards in my first explanation to the owner and corrected it after re-reading the planner - the earlier framing of 'rank it last for repair' assumed a repair budget that does not exist.)

THE DEFECT THE RULING EXPOSES. Which hits got forgiven was decided by DOCUMENT ORDER - whichever the scanner walked past first - with nothing to do with severity. So a page could keep both of its `x_not_y` constructions (the shape the owner actually complained about) purely because they appeared near the top, and spend the gate's effort rewriting two `rather than`s further down. That is the ruling inverted, and it was arbitrary rather than wrong-by-design: reverse the paragraph order on the same page and you get the opposite outcome.

THE CHANGE. Only a MILD shape may spend the budget. `rather_than` is mild; every other shape (`x_not_y`, `not_x_but_y`, `staccato`, `negative_reveal`) is sharp and is now always repaired in a non-headline field. `rather than` remains FULLY DETECTED, still counts toward `page_hits` and the density signal, and is still repaired once the page's tolerance is spent. Headline behaviour is unchanged - always repaired, any shape, regardless of budget.

WHY A FUNCTION ON THE VOCABULARY RATHER THAN A CONFIG KEY. Which shapes are mild is a judgement about English recorded as an owner ruling, not an operational dial an operator should turn per site. `page_budget` remains the dial. This also keeps the action at 4 config keys, well inside the WFA-013 optional-key budget of 10.

TWO CARRIED COUNTERS, AND THIS IS THE ONLY SUBTLE PART. The budget is per PAGE, carried across sections in the marker. It was seeded from `page_hits`, which counts EVERY shape. If only mild shapes may spend the budget but the seed still counts sharp ones, a sharp hit in section 1 silently eats section 3's forgiveness - the same inversion the ruling is about, one section removed. So `mild_hits` is carried separately alongside `page_hits`, both excluded from `stampCopyGate`'s copy the same way. A test pins exactly this: a sharp-only section must leave the following section's budget untouched.

SCALE, stated because it bounds the blast radius: `rather_than` is 71% of all gate rewrites and appears in 43% of writer sections (measured 2026-08-23/24). So this changes which shape most of the gate's traffic belongs to, and moving any shape in or out of the mild set later is a large change dressed as a one-line edit.

plan.summary: Make the copy gate's page budget shape-aware: only a mild shape (rather_than, per the owner's D3 ruling) may consume it; sharp shapes are always repaired. Carry the mild count across sections separately from page_hits. Three new tests, two mutations.

edits.rationale: The classification belongs with the shape vocabulary it classifies, not buried in the planner. A set rather than an equality test so a second mild shape is one line and so it reads as a policy list. Doc comment carries the ruling, what it is NOT (neither of D3's two options), and the 71%/43% scale so nobody widens it casually.
One condition. A sharp shape no longer reaches the budget branch and falls through to become a target. plan.mildHits counts what the budget counts, so it can be carried.

The per-page carry. Mirrors the existing page_hits pair exactly, and stampCopyGate must skip mild_hits for the same reason it skips page_hits (both are owned per-section). Seeding the budget from page_hits instead would let a sharp hit in an earlier section eat a later section's forgiveness.

edits.symbol: three new tests + two re-pointed fixtures
edits.rationale: New: TestOnlyAMildShapeCanSpendThePageBudget (fixture ordered so document order works AGAINST the desired outcome - the sharp hits come first, so under the old rule they would have consumed the budget and survived); TestTheMildBudgetCarriesAcrossSectionsWithoutSharpHitsEatingIt (the two-counter property); TestAMildShapeInAHeadlineIsStillAlwaysRepaired (unchanged behaviour, pinned because it sits directly beside the edited branch). RE-POINTED, and flagged inline as changed: TestExemptHitsDoNotConsumeTheBudget and TestBudgetIsPerPageNotPerSection used sharp fixtures to demonstrate budget consumption, which a sharp shape can no longer do. Their subjects (an exempt hit must not eat the budget; the budget is per page) are untouched by the ruling and their assertions are unchanged - only the shape of the fixture moved.

grounded_in: Owner ruling, 2026-08-24, verbatim: "rather than is a little bit of a tic."

The budget's real semantics, from planNegationRepairs: `if !headline { used++; if used <= budget { plan.withinBudget++; continue } }` — the `continue` SKIPS the hit, so the budget tolerates rather than caps. Everything past it becomes a target.
The five shapes, from the scanner's table: x_not_y, not_x_but_y, staccato, rather_than, negative_reveal.

Scale: rather_than was 29 of 41 recorded rewrites (71%) and both recorded rejections; measured over live copy_gate markers 2026-08-23. It appears in 43% of writer sections (the lane's original census).
The two-counter necessity: `used := alreadyUsed` was seeded from pageHitsSoFar(params), which reads the marker's `page_hits` — a total over every shape, incremented for headline hits too.

Mutation evidence, both directions: reverting the mildness gate to `if !headline {` fails TestOnlyAMildShapeCanSpendThePageBudget with 'x_not_y targets = 0, want 2'; separately making NegationShapeIsMild return true for everything fails it identically. So neither the call site nor the classification is decorative.
Config-key count: the action declares 4 (content_from, brief_fields, page_budget, ai_service), so adding none keeps it far inside the WFA-013 budget of 10.
plan.risks:
MORE REPAIRS ON SHARP SHAPES, which is the intent and is the main behavioural risk. A page with several sharp non-headline constructions previously kept two and now keeps none. Sharp shapes were ~29% of hits, and pages with 3+ sharp non-headline hits are uncommon, but this does raise repair volume on exactly the pages the owner complained about — and every repair is a chance for the model to introduce new phrasing. The gate's existing defences still apply unchanged (banned-claims scan before structure, AcceptNegationRewrite, and the rejection log).

THE TOLERANCE CAN NOW GO UNSPENT. A page with only sharp hits forgives nothing and repairs everything. That is the ruling, but it means `withinBudget` will read 0 more often, and anyone reading that field as 'the gate is being conservative' will misread it. It is now specifically 'mild hits forgiven'.

TWO RE-POINTED TESTS, declared rather than quiet: two existing tests asserted that sharp shapes get forgiveness — the old policy. I changed their FIXTURES (sharp -> mild) and left every assertion intact, with an inline note saying so. 'I changed the test to make it pass' is the shape to distrust, so the note names what moved and why the test's actual subject is unaffected.

NOT ADDRESSED: `staccato` is classed sharp by omission and I have no measurement of its frequency — it may deserve the mild set too, but guessing is how a policy list rots. If it turns out common, it needs its own ruling, not an edit.

INERT UNTIL THE NEXT ROLL — Go. The D3 ruling has no effect on served pages until the chassis rebuilds.
